gaps.lead: He couldn't swim until he was twenty.
gaps.sentence: He ___ swim until he was twenty.
gaps.explanation: couldn't = was not able to (general ability in the past).

gaps.lead: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.
gaps.explanation: keep something to yourself = tell nobody.

gaps.lead: He no longer thinks he can find a job before the end of the year.
gaps.sentence: He has given ___ a job before the end of the year.
gaps.explanation: 'No longer thinks he can find' becomes 'has given up hope of finding'.

gaps.lead: 'I've never been to Asia,' she told me.
gaps.sentence: She told me that ___ to Asia.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect shifts to past perfect in reported speech.

gaps.lead: I always hated pasta when I was a child, but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.sentence: I ___ pasta when I was a child but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.explanation: 'used to + infinitive' describes a past state or habit that is no longer true.

gaps.lead: They won't let you in without a ticket.
gaps.explanation: let somebody do → be allowed to do: won't be allowed in.
